The absorber achieves more than 90% co-polarization absorption from 5.6 GHz to 9.1 GHz for both TE and TM polarizations at normal incidence.
The absorber thickness is 3.2 mm, which is 12.7 times thinner than the wavelength at the center frequency.
Rotating the U-shaped resonator by 45° enables broadband absorption and equalizes TE and TM absorption rates.
The unit cell consists of a copper UUSR on a 3.2 mm thick FR4 dielectric backed by a copper ground plane.
Three near-unity absorption peaks occur at 5.86 GHz, 7.16 GHz, and 8.82 GHz.
Electric fields concentrate around specific regions of the UUSR, while magnetic fields arise from anti-parallel currents between the resonator and ground plane.
The absorber maintains over 50% absorption up to 40° oblique incidence for both polarizations.
The operational bandwidth-to-thickness ratio is 6.43, outperforming several other absorbers.
The absorber is fabricated using conventional PCB technology and tested in an anechoic chamber.
Measurement results closely match simulation results, with minor frequency shifts due to dielectric permittivity variations.
The absorber is designed for co-polarization absorption and does not significantly absorb cross-polarized waves.
The FR4 dielectric has a permittivity of 3.92 and loss tangent of 0.025.
The copper used has an electrical conductivity of 5.8 × 10^7 S/m and thickness of 0.017 mm.
The unit cells are arranged in a periodic array with a period of 15 mm.
The design uses a transmission line model to match the complex sheet impedance to free space impedance for perfect absorption.
Increasing dielectric thickness does not necessarily increase bandwidth; impedance matching is critical.
The absorber can reduce electromagnetic interference caused by metallic objects inside radomes.
The UUSR shape provides capacitive surface impedance characterized as Z = 1 / (jωC).
The design is competitive for applications in the GHz frequency range, especially for radar stealth and EMC.
Future work includes making the absorber flexible and optimizing for nonplanar surfaces.
